channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] Caretaker PM Netanyahu expected to escalate violence, as EU sanctions talk on hold until new Israeli government formed
item.description: Israel's "vibrant democracy" gave the most votes to a man wanted for war crimes by the International Criminal Court in The Hague and accused of perpetrating genocide by UN experts, posing questions on whether Israeli society is aligned with EU values.

item.title: [DW] Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
item.description: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

item.title: [EU Observer] Digital panopticon: ‘When you work faster, you have to work even faster’ Amazon workers tell MEPs on AI work surveillance
item.description: Seven MEPs from the employment committee visited Amazon warehouses in Germany and Poland this week - ahead of the EU Commission’s Quality Jobs Act proposal expected in December.

item.title: [Financial Times] Fed to decide on interest rates as US midterm elections loom
item.description: Policymakers weigh whether to deliver back-to-back increases in effort to tame inflation exacerbated by Donald Trump’s war against Iran

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘I don’t care’ about the associate membership label row: Lead MEP Javier Moreno Sánchez on upcoming EU-Canada summit
item.description: “Everybody's focusing on the legal basis of Ursula von der Leyen’s associate membership announcement, but frankly I don't care,” says the European Parliament lead on Canada. He hopes digital trade, critical raw materials and Erasmus+ will be prioritised in talks this week in Montreal.

item.title: [Financial Times] At least 68 killed in collision of high-speed trains in Spain
item.description: Crash near Toledo south of Madrid follows death of 46 in Andalusia rail accident in January

item.title: [Euractiv] Netherlands to give Ukraine ‘whatever we have’ in air defence supplies
item.description: Jetten says he is reaching out to partners to ask them to do more for Kyiv

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin faces African anger in Moscow on ‘coercive’ recruits to Russian army in Ukraine
item.description: Russia's hopes of using a summit with African leaders to increase its influence on the continent have been hit by African anger about the fate of their men recruited by the Russian army.

item.title: [Euractiv] Liese seeks centrist deal on EU carbon pricing reform
item.description: EPP's lead negotiator favours broad compromise in the political centre over an alliance with the far right

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainian soldier’s frontline phone messages show tragic human cost of maintaining resistance against Russian forces in Kostiantynivka (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,707)
item.description: Russia claims it has captured the city of Kostiantynivka, but the fighting continues, as chronicled in messages to his wife by 42-year-old Hennadii Osadchyi.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Billionaires shatter spending record to fight California wealth tax
item.description: It’s a striking and historic show of unity from a notoriously hard-to-organize donor class, a POLITICO analysis shows.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK vows defense spending boost by 2030 but dodges hard questions
item.description: John Healey committed to spending 3% of GDP on the nation's defences by 2030 but declined to say where he would find the money.

item.title: [Euractiv] UK to unveil plan for NATO’s 3.5% target next year
item.description: Government seeks to attract private investment as defence spending rises

item.title: [EU Observer] Frontex gets 17,000 extra officers for deportations while human-rights monitoring suffers downgrade
item.description: The European Commission says Frontex's human rights monitoring won't fundamentally change, citing the need to avoid duplication with EU states. But the text of its proposal suggests otherwise.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU set to scrap ‘associate member’ offer for Canada
item.description: A group of countries including Germany, Greece and France all objected to mentioning associate membership in a joint EU-Canada statement.

item.title: [Financial Times] Bolsonaro lands in US after fleeing Brazil
item.description: Losing presidential candidate and son of jailed ex-president Jair Bolsonaro left Brazil after being ordered to hand over his passports

item.title: [Euractiv] SAFE leftovers set at €21bn after Commission clears Hungarian plan
item.description: The new call will be released before the end of the year

item.title: [Financial Times] The fear factor giving Netanyahu the edge
item.description: Despite liberal hopes, the veteran leader appears to have a path back to government after Israel’s vote

item.title: [Euractiv] Berlin nails new wording to unblock EU-Canada stalemate
item.description: Germany has resisted offering 'associate member' status to Canada as EU talks went to the wire

item.title: [Politico Europe] Healey targets Brits’ energy costs, raids banks in first budget
item.description: Britain's chancellor unveils first budget of the Andy Burnham era — as watchdog reveals decade-long pressure on living standards.

item.title: [Euractiv] Bulgaria boosts defences as drones strike another Black Sea ship
item.description: Sofia will also buy 32 VL MICA air-defence missiles for its navy with EU defence loans

item.title: [Politico Europe] Weidels Wandel
item.description: Wie opportunistisch agiert Alice Weidel an der Parteispitze? Geleakte E-Mails aus den Jahren 2015 bis 2017 offenbaren einen radikalen Kurswechsel im Umgang mit Björn Höcke und zeigen detailliert, wie aus scharfer Distanzierung und Parteiausschlussforderungen ein strategisches Bündnis mit dem extremen Flügel wurde. Die brisanten Dokumente werfen zudem ein neues Licht auf illegale Wahlkampfspenden aus der […]

item.title: [EU Observer] Knife-edge EU Council methane vote could hinge on commission action plan
item.description: EU member states remain split between a one-year and a three-year delay of the bloc's methane rules, with some saying that a commission action plan could tip the balance.

item.title: [EU Observer] How the rescue of 28 people from a makeshift dinghy in a stormy Mediterranean unfolded – exposing the lethal reality of EU border policy
item.description: A small, homemade, dinghy hoped to escape the deadly EU-sponsored Libyan coastguard by making its way north during one of the stormiest seasons in the Mediterranean Sea. Their successful rescue by volunteers contrasts with the reception they received from Italian authorities, prior to even touching European land.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK’s Healey cracks down on VAT-shirking online sellers
item.description: Move to close a loophole brings Britain closer to approaches adopted in Switzerland.

item.title: [Euractiv] INTERVIEW: Amazon visit shows need for workplace rules on AI, says MEP
item.description: Algorithmic management poses a key challenge, says MEP Li Andersson

item.title: [Politico Europe] Berlin startet KI-Überwachung am Kottbusser Tor
item.description: 30 Kameras sollen ab November automatisch Gewalttaten und Notfälle erkennen. Ganz so anonym, wie zunächst dargestellt, ist die Überwachung allerdings nicht.

item.title: [Euractiv] Zelenskyy fears new Yalta at Russia-China-US summit
item.description: Ukraine warns against a repeat of the 1945 superpower carve-up that created the Iron Curtain

item.title: [Euractiv] EMA urged to step up as trust in US regulator falters
item.description: US anti-vaccine rhetoric has had a ripple effect across much of the world

item.title: [Politico Europe] Zelenskyy defends leaders of Finland and Norway over Putin talks
item.description: Some European governments have criticized Alexander Stubb and Jonas Gahr Støre for breaking ranks and calling the Russian leader directly.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Eurovision confirms candidates for 2027 — but 2 EU countries are still on the fence
item.description: Ireland, the Netherlands and Iceland will once again boycott the competition next year.

item.title: [Euractiv] Sánchez’s wife sues Spanish opposition over AI deepfake
item.description: Case filed over 'identity theft' but also touches on EU tech rulebook

item.title: [Euractiv] Fatal high-speed train crash in Spain
item.description: Second deadly high-speed train accident in nine months in the middle of an electoral race

item.title: [Euractiv] Europe’s circular economy challenge is not a lack of ambition. It’s a lack of systems [Promoted Content]
item.description: By prioritising renovation, reuse, recycled materials and harmonised rules that keep valuable products and materials in circulation longer, Europe can reduce resource dependence, strengthen competitiveness and create regulatory certainty to scale circular business models.

item.title: [Politico Europe] At least 68 people die in major Spanish train crash
item.description: The collision brings back memories of the January train crash in Adamuz, which killed 46 people.

item.title: [DW] EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

item.title: [Financial Times] Why even America’s ‘haves’ are feeling the squeeze
item.description: Rising costs everywhere from insurance to lawn care mean almost half of US homeowners lack financial breathing room

item.title: [Financial Times] Zelenskyy opens door to security guarantees for Russia
item.description: Ukrainian president acknowledges Moscow could also receive security guarantees as part of peace deal

item.title: [Financial Times] Netanyahu ahead but no clear winner in Israeli election
item.description: Prime minister urges rivals to join Jewish coalition and shun Arab parties as neither bloc set for majority

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: is the European Commission’s climate resilience plan enough?
item.description: The European Commission has unveiled its plan to help Europe adapt to climate change. But as extreme heat and climate disasters become the norm, the plan offers very few binding commitments.

item.title: [DW] Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
item.description: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

item.title: [Euractiv] Netanyahu bloc leads as Israeli votes counted, but no majority
item.description: Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict

item.title: [Euractiv] Serbian police kill underage attacker outside Israeli embassy
item.description: The interior minister said the terrorism threat level had been raised to its highest

item.title: [DW] Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
item.description: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

item.title: [Euractiv] FIREPOWER: Kubilius co-chairs dialogue on refineries
item.description: In today's edition: naval warfare, PAC-3 maintenance, Ukraine

item.title: [EU Observer] Secrecy Tracker: Media groups urge von der Leyen to tackle EU secrecy as watchdog probes Gaza documents
item.description: Publishers and media organisations, including EUobserver, urge the European Commission to improve transparency as concerns grow over restricted access to EU documents, while secrecy surrounding Gaza funding has been picked up by the EU ombudsman.

item.title: [Financial Times] The globetrotting Trump brothers
item.description: The president’s sons Donald Jr and Eric have met world leaders and foreign officials while building a lucrative web of financial interests

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic’s seven founders tighten grip ahead of blockbuster IPO
item.description: From a rebellion at OpenAI to building the Claude-maker, the new billionaires are betting their future on staying united

item.title: [EU Observer] Revealed: New data shows Big Tech lobbying pushing EU towards sweeping data-protection rollback
item.description: New report points to extensive industry access to European politicians, as governments back changes to data protection rules in the name of AI competitiveness.

item.title: [Financial Times] Washington discusses Russian deals for US oil majors in Ukraine peace talks
item.description: White House proposes renewed postwar business ties in an effort to bring President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s centre parties are collapsing – and, for the first time, the far-right are collaborating, rather than fighting
item.description: Opinion polling from the Pew Research Center found that 69 percent of the French population is dissatisfied with democracy, Italy 62 percent, Poland 47 percent and Spain 68 percent. All are facing upcoming elections.

item.title: [EU Observer] Finnish president Stubb joins list of EU leaders seeking to tame Putin, in a 90-minute Kremlin phone call that caused a rift with Denmark
item.description: The Finnish-Norwegian call was "not coordinated with any of us [allies]" in advance, said Denmark's Mette Frederiksen on Tuesday - directly contradicting Finland's Alexander Stubb and Norway's Jonas Gahr Støre. "I really don't understand what these two countries think can be achieved this way," she said.

item.title: [EU Observer] Two graphs and one map show that Russia is not currently winning the war (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,706)
item.description: Analysts tracking satellite images, daily engagements and shifting frontlines say the war has frozen into a deadly stalemate.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU plans massive investment in Australia’s critical minerals to cut dependence on China
item.description: Australia has announced plans to overhaul its national critical minerals strategy, and the EU says it wants to invest 'massively' in refining and processing.

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
item.description: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

item.title: [DW] In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.title: [DW] Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
item.description: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
item.description: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.
